transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-01
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM) — Aaron Patel (Lyra), Selene Gomez (Lyra), Markus Voss (Lyra), Priya Rao (Lyra)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align on network/VPC, SSO, compliance, and pilot success criteria. SE to run perf/cost estimate. Next steps and action items summarized at end.

00:00 Maya: ok everyone thanks for joining, we'll get started. hi Aaron, Selene, Markus, priya from Lyra, thanks for time. i'm maya chen, i'll be your AE, with david our solutions engineer and priya kapoor on success.
00:20 Aaron: yeah thanks maya, excited to get this moving. timeline's tight—we're hoping pilot by end of Q2, so basically three months. primary goals are onboarding low-latency inference for chat assistants and moving our internal ticket triage to embeddings.
00:40 David: great, that helps. quick clarification, pilot scope — do you want hosted or private? or hybrid? last we spoke it was leaning private VPC with dedicated capacity for compliance.
01:05 Aaron: correct, legal pushed back on hosted due to data residency and egress concerns. we need VPC peering and KMS integration, ideally HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest.
01:22 Markus: and from security side we need SOC2 type 2 evidence, iso 27001, and audit log retention for 3 years. also whitelisting for egress, and allowlist of IPs. we may require a vulnerability scan before staging.
01:40 Maya: understood, we can share SOC2+ISO pack. redwood private supports KMS/HSM, and we have audit logs — david will walk through options in a bit. for peering we support aws vpc peering and transit gateway setups, also on-prem options via direct connect, depending on your infra.
02:05 Selene: quick note — our infra team uses kubernetes for orchestration and we have existing nvidia VMs; can Redwood integrate with our k8s cluster or do you expect us to use redwood private appliances?
02:28 David: good question — for private there are two paths: (1) managed private control plane where you keep data in your VPC and we deploy inference nodes in your account, or (2) on-prem package where we deliver a containerized runtime run in your k8s cluster. each has tradeoffs for latency, ops overhead, and patching.
02:54 Selene: container option sounds interest — how's KV cache handled there, and will we lose batching efficiency?
03:08 David: we have an embeddable cache layer that preserves the KV cache locally, but batching depends on topology. if you're using many small replicas in k8s, you can enable local batching with a small proxy. real-world latency numbers will vary — i'll put numbers in the perf worksheet.
03:32 Aaron: perfect. one red flag from procurement was cost unpredictability — can you do dedicated capacity with fixed monthly commit to smooth costs?
03:45 Maya: yes we have Redwood Dedicated — committed pools with monthly/annual contracts. those give predictable throughput and lower unit cost. we can model both hosted per-token and dedicated monthly for your expected QPS.
04:02 Priya (CSM): for onboarding we'll prepare a ramp plan: sandbox access, data onboarding, eval prompt sets, and a go-no-go checklist. we usually do weekly syncs during pilot.
04:20 Markus: for compliance we'll want a flowchart: who touches keys, where logs are stored, who has console access, and SSO mapping (roles). do you support SAML/SSO with role-mapping?
04:37 Maya: yes SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning — we'll share the SSO guide. we also support fine-grained RBAC and can integrate with your IdP for role sync.
05:00 Aaron: on the latency vs cost tradeoff: our user journeys need sub-200ms median for short prompts. is that achievable with quantized models on dedicated GPUs?
05:15 David: sub-200ms median is challenging at high concurrency but possible with right model + quantization + batching config. low-seqlen short prompts on Llama2-chat-13B quantized to 4-bit on A10/A100 class can get there for single-token throughput; but depends on payload and streaming. i'll recommend model variant in the perf estimate.
05:40 Selene: does Redwood handle model patching/rollouts? we want canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller model if capacity spikes.
05:52 Maya: yes we have rollout policies: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to pinned variants. console lets you configure percent traffic and automatic rollback on errors.
06:10 Markus: clarify data retention — we will not permit retention of raw customer content in hosted logs; do you offer 'no retention' options in private?
06:23 Priya (CSM): in private deployments data stays in customer VPC and you control retention. hosted has configurable retention policies and opt-out agreements for enterprise.
06:38 Aaron: good. for the pilot success criteria — what metrics should we agree to measure?
06:48 Maya: propose: latency (p50/p95), token cost per call, accuracy on your eval set (F1/Precision), and uptime/SLA adherence. also operational metrics: cache hit rate, queue depth, and cost per 1M tokens.
07:10 Aaron: sounds good. we'll share an eval prompt set next week.

07:40 David: i'm going to run a quick topology example — imagine a VPC with private subnets for inference + NAT for model updates. we'd do KMS asymmetric key import, use private endpoints for telemetry, and disable public outbound except to model registries. latency to your frontends will be one RTT inside your region — we can place inference nodes in the same AZ for lowest latency.
08:20 Selene: are there network firewall rules to open? what's required?
08:28 David: minimal: allow outbound to registry endpoints (or provide offline image), allow VPC peering endpoints, and open health check ports between load balancers and nodes. we'll send a checklist.
08:45 Priya Rao (Lyra): small ask — our product ops want a runbook for incident handoff. who triages alerts and how do we get paged?
08:56 Priya (CSM): we do on-call integration; for private we can forward alerts to your pagerduty and include runbooks and escalation paths. we'll include suggested runbooks in the docs.
09:15 Markus: security question — for HSM-backed keys is bring-your-own-key supported and can audit log key use?
09:27 Maya: yes BYOK is supported and uses KMS APIs; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and include key usage. there is some obfuscation of derived tokens but the logs show timestamps and request IDs.
09:45 Aaron: procurement asked about pricing model tiers and any overage protections.
09:55 Maya: we'll provide a pricing sheet — dedicated pools, monthly commit tiers, and overage caps. we can do a blended price for the pilot to keep costs predictable.
10:12 Selene: what's the onboarding timeline from sandbox to pilot if we start now?
10:19 Priya (CSM): typical ramp: day 0 sign-off and admin access, week 1 sandbox and access, week 2 model onboarding and evals, weeks 3-4 pilot performance tuning, week 6 pilot go/no-go. since you're aiming for end of Q2, we have room.
10:40 Aaron: okay. can you speak to data residency across regions? we have users in eu and us — want regional serving.
10:50 David: we support regional deployments and smart routing; requests can be routed to region-specific inference pools to satisfy residency. cross-region replication of KV cache is optional and disabled by default.
11:10 Maya: quick housekeeping — we'll create a shared drive folder and Slack channel. david will own the perf worksheet and priya csm will own runbook and SSO docs.

11:30 Customer deep-dive questions
11:35 Aaron: on the evaluation set—are there tooling recommendations for label collection and A/B evals?
11:45 David: we recommend pairing our eval harness with your telemetry exports; simpler is to sample 1% of production traffic and run offline scoring. we can attach our eval script that computes F1/precision/recall for classification tasks.
12:12 Selene: do you have prebuilt connectors for our data sources — we use gcs and a proprietary ticketing db.
12:24 Maya: connectors for s3/gcs and generic DB ingestion pipelines exist; for the ticketing system we may need a small adaptor. we can scope that in the POC.
12:40 Markus: another compliance ask — can we have restricted console access per team? e.g., devs can deploy models but only security has key export permission.
12:52 David: yes RBAC roles can be scoped. we support role templates and custom roles; actions like key management are separated.
13:10 Aaron: what's the backup/restore story for model artifacts and custom tokenizers?
13:20 David: artifacts are stored in your object store (you can choose), snapshots can be configured nightly, and we support restore into staging. custom tokenizers are included in the model bundle.
13:40 Selene: about model quantization — do you handle retraining or we do quantization ourselves?
13:48 David: we provide quantization tooling and recommended configurations; we don't retrain models for you, but we can run quantization passes and evaluate quality/latency tradeoffs.

14:15 Cross-talk / brief pause
14:30 Priya (Lyra): sorry, quick interruption — legal asked if Redwood has an incident response SLA and a breach notification window.
14:40 Maya: yes we have incident response commitments in the enterprise agreement; breach notification is typically 72 hours for covered incidents, with escalation paths documented. we'll include the security playbook.
14:58 Markus: ok good

15:10 Technical clarifications
15:15 David: i'll highlight one nuance — KV cache warmup. during pilot you may see higher latency on cold starts; we recommend synthetic warm-up traffic and measuring cache-hit ratio. we have cache prefill tooling for common prompts.
15:42 Selene: what's the recommended model for chat memory and token pruning?
15:50 David: we recommend prefix caching for system messages and aggressive pruning for long-running chats; we can provide heuristics and default TTLs.
16:05 Aaron: for the POC do you suggest using Redwood hosted for faster iteration and then move to private for production? any gotchas?
16:20 Maya: many customers start hosted for speed and then shift to private with the same API; the main gotcha is keying and audit differences and possibly tokenization differences if you change model variants — david can note compatibility checks.
16:40 David: yes validate prompts across model variants — we'll include compatibility matrix.

17:05 Pilot SLOs and expectations
17:12 Priya (CSM): propose weekly check-ins, daily slacks during s/cutover, and a go/no-go meeting after 4 weeks with recorded metrics. we'll also set up alert thresholds.
17:30 Aaron: ok that's fine. who will be our point of contact for emergency issues during pilot?
17:40 Maya: primary contact will be priya kapoor (CSM) for coordination, and david for technical escalation. i'll remain involved for contract conversations.
17:55 Priya Kapoor: i'll send initial calendar invites for weekly syncs and add the slack channel.

18:10 Final recap
18:15 Maya: recap — action items: share SSO and VPC checklists, perf worksheet, SOC2/ISO docs, and pilot runbook. redwood to estimate latency and cost based on sample trace david will request.
18:30 Aaron: next steps look good, we'll send eval prompt set and sample trace by 2027-03-03.
18:45 Maya: i'll follow up with docs and proposed dates for the SE deep-dive. thanks everyone.
